title: Five port layouts, generated from one traceable model.
summary: A rectangular reference, earlier exhaust, taper, split exhaust and staged transfers now form a numerically verified synthetic geometry comparison. Their differences are explicit; physical port design and candidate CAD acceptance remain open.
evidence: Generated and numerically verified synthetic geometry · no candidate CAD acceptance
thumbnailAlt: Original developed-wall polygons for the tapered exhaust and common transfer windows.
heroAlt: Original developed-wall polygons for the tapered exhaust and common transfer windows.
heroCaption: Original G001-03 source geometry, unmodified. Exhaust is orange; transfers are cyan. The developed circumferential coordinate is s; z is positive toward the crank. This is synthetic geometry, not a released cylinder drawing.

sections.title: Generate a family that can be compared
sections.text: The new generator produced five complete exhaust-and-transfer configurations from structured parameters. It retains actual polygon contours, separate port identities and a common nominal piston mechanism. These are synthetic developed-wall designs, with rectangular and tapered primitives, separated lobes and staged windows. Installed piston-edge, deck, ring and duct geometry remain unresolved.

figure.alt: Rectangular reference developed wall with orange exhaust and cyan transfers.
figure.caption: G001-01: the common reference. The seam splits the exhaust across the left and right edges of the developed wall; those pieces belong to the same cylindrical layout.

sections.title: Separate opening time from contour progression
sections.text: Reference exhaust opens at 90° and closes at 270°. G001-02 opens at 82° and closes at 278°, while its maximum exposed area also rises from 359.451897 to 438.145989 mm². G001-03 retains the reference events but narrows the roof to one quarter of its floor width. Its maximum aperture is 224.657436 mm². An event time alone cannot describe the complete opening history.

figure.alt: All five original exhaust area curves versus crank angle in degrees, with developed open area in square millimetres.
figure.caption: Saved aperture overlay reused from the later G001-B comparison of the same unchanged contours. Geometry against crank angle is shared; the original G001 geometric time-area context was 10,000 rpm, while G001-B uses its own 3,000 rpm experiment clock. G001-01 and G001-05 coincide.

sections.title: Keep the split geometry visible
sections.text: G001-04 separates the exhaust into lobes around an illustrative bridge occupying 25% of the outer reference width. Its maximum combined exhaust aperture is 269.588923 mm², with the same 90°/270° events as the reference. The bridge changes the geometric opening; ring support, thermal survival and manufacturability were not tested.

figure.alt: Original split exhaust developed-wall polygons with a geometric gap and common transfer windows.
figure.caption: Exact source polygons, with the cylindrical seam retained. This geometric gap does not establish a physical bridge design or a flow benefit.

sections.title: Stage the transfers instead
sections.text: G001-05 retains the reference exhaust and introduces early and late transfer windows. The early stage opens at 116°; the later stage opens at 137.867190666° and closes at 222.132809334°. Combined maximum transfer aperture is 117.566773 mm², compared with 188.106836 mm² for the common transfers. Sequencing is demonstrated geometrically; directed scavenging is not.

figure.alt: Original early and late transfer polygons in cyan with the reference orange exhaust.
figure.caption: Two stages are actual separate polygons in the saved model. No replacement rectangular approximation is used.

sections.title: Verify differences without choosing a winner
sections.text: All five initial configurations passed; there was no optimization sweep or fallback search. Independent qualification recorded 7,607 checks, followed by 47,553 separate saved-data checks. All ten candidate pairs passed the frozen geometric-distinctness rules. These checks establish bounded numerical behaviour and traceable differences, rather than physical superiority.

figure.alt: Original all-five transfer exposed-area curves; the common four candidates overlap and staged G001-05 is distinct.
figure.caption: Saved G001-B aperture overlay. G001-01 through G001-04 intentionally share one transfer history; source draw order leaves the violet G001-04 line visible. The pink G001-05 trace shows the staged opening.

sections.title: Carry the contours into flow, keep CAD separate
sections.text: The next accepted study uses these same five contours in a prescribed-reservoir flow comparison. Read From port shape to synthetic gas exchange ↗. That new numerical layer does not change the CAD outcome: the separate Rhino startup attempt failed its execution gate before persistence/readback acceptance, and the candidate-CAD stage remained blocked. No candidate became CAD verified and no new native candidate file was accepted.
